summary: Service-account SSO assertion algorithm mismatch prevents runbook token issuance
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 09:14 UTC, internal automation runbooks that use a service-account SAML assertion to request short-lived access tokens began failing with 401/invalid_grant errors. Impact: Several on-call runbooks that automatically rotate credentials and execute emergency mitigation (DB-failover, kafka-reassign) could not obtain tokens, causing manual intervention and increased MTTR. Scope: Affects service-account based runbook flows across multiple teams in prod-us-west only; interactive user SSO unaffected.

Observed behavior: Token-exchange endpoint returns HTTP 401 with body 'invalid_grant: unsupported assertion algorithm' when presented with the assertion from the service-account SAML app. This causes the runbook worker to abort token acquisition and mark the job failed.

Business impact: Two automated failover runbooks failed to execute in a recent incident, requiring on-call engineers to run steps manually. This elevated operational load during an unrelated platform degradation and extended recovery time by ~22 minutes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Generate SAML assertion for the affected service account using the current service-bot signing key and algorithm.
3) Observe 401 invalid_grant with message referencing unsupported assertion algorithm
logs: 2026-03-12T09:14:03Z runbook-worker[pid=2245] ERROR token-exchange: grant failed status=401 body="{"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"unsupported assertion algorithm: ES384"}"
2026-03-12T09:14:03Z auth-service[pid=812] WARN saml-validator: received assertion alg=ES384 expected=RS256 subject=svc-runbook-rotate
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: recent key rotation on the service-bot signing key introduced a different signing algorithm (ES384) that the token-exchange service does not accept for service-account assertions.
Confirmed: Okta SAML app for svc-runbook now signs assertions using ECDSA (ES384). Audit shows rotation performed by automation on 2026-03-11 23:58 UTC (PR infra/keys#452).

Auth stack behavior: token-exchange validation component explicitly checks for RS256 and rejects other alg values. Historical reason: token-exchange uses legacy RS256-only verifier to simplify JWK cache logic created in 2024.
Risk: Accepting additional algorithms without careful validation could open signature confusion issues; need to restrict to known key IDs and algorithms for each service-account.
Repro test: Updated local token-exchange verifier to accept ES384 and re-ran runbook assertion; token issued successfully and runbook executed.
Temporary mitigation considered: revert SAML app signing algorithm back to RS256 (Okta app setting) or patch token-exchange to accept ES algorithms for specific service-account kid.
Decision: Apply hotfix to token-exchange to accept ES384 for the specific kid used by svc-runbook, plus revert automation that rotated the key to ES algorithms until a compatibility plan is in place.
comments: Support (Aisha Kapoor) - 2026-03-12: Customer-facing impact internal - runbooks failing to get tokens; opened ticket and paged infra owners. See slack #oncall-ops thread G12345.

SRE (Samira Patel) - 2026-03-12: Reproduced locally, saw alg=ES384 rejected by token-exchange. Creating PR to add allowed-algs per-kid mapping. Working on hotfix. linked PR: https://github.com/redwoodinc/infra/pull/789
Security (Diego Morales) - 2026-03-12: Flag: ensure new verifier checks kid and origin of JWK before accepting ES alg. We should not broadly enable additional algs for all tenants.

Infra Automation (Liam Chen) - 2026-03-12: The key-rotation job mistakenly selected the new ECDSA key from the KMS keyring; rolling back rotation to previous RS256 key now. See commit: https://github.com/redwoodinc/infra/commit/abc123

SRE (Samira Patel) - 2026-03-13: Hotfix deployed to token-exchange in prod-us-west: added per-kid allowed_algs mapping and ES384 acceptance for kid 'svc-runbook-key-v3'. Runbooks resumed normal operation at 2026-03-13T04:22Z. Monitoring for 6h.
Aisha Kapoor - 2026-03-13: Monitoring confirms automated runbooks executed successfully; closing blocker if no regressions by EOD.
resolution: Hotfix applied: token-exchange service updated to perform per-kid algorithm allowlist and accept ES384 for the specific service-account key (kid 'svc-runbook-key-v3'). The automation key-rotation job was reverted to reuse the RS256 key while a compatibility plan is developed. Runbooks resumed automated execution by 2026-03-13T04:22Z. Follow-up: create a formal key-rotation compatibility test, update runbook onboarding doc to include alg expectations, and schedule a security review before enabling ECDSA keys for service-accounts.
